clue.text: Overtaking Western man is just a fad

parts.note: overtaking another car is passing it
a man is referred to as him

explanation.surface: A driver's habit of overtaking cowboys is dismissed as a mere craze.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleeting fancy that soon fades is a craze, exactly what a fad is.

clue.text: Writer goes to Jerusalem boarding-house

parts.note: a pen is the thing one writes with
Sion (Zion) is a poetic name for Jerusalem

explanation.surface: An author travels to the Holy City and stays in a guest house.
explanation.walkthrough: PEN then SION; Sion is an old spelling of Zion, the hill and city of Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: A pension, in the continental sense, is a small hotel offering board and lodging.

clue.text: Meet requirements to be employed in the forces

explanation.surface: Doing what is required by joining the army.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet requirements is to be adequate for a purpose, and to work as a soldier is to do military service.

clue.text: Better if I am put to the test

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm, giving these two letters
to prove something is to test it, as in proving ground

explanation.surface: A suggestion that being examined will make one a finer person.
explanation.definitionFit: To better something is to make it superior or enhance it, a verb sense.

clue.text: From them brandy is permitted to enter mouths

indicators.note: one word is said to go into another, so the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: gob is slang for mouth
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: Spirits are allowed to pass the lips of drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' signals the container. The definition is cryptic: these are the vessels from which brandy is drunk, and 'mouths' is slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Goblets are stemmed drinking glasses, the vessels a spirit is sipped from.

clue.text: Penitent habit

parts.note: habit read as clothing rather than custom: a coarse garment worn next to the skin by someone doing penance

explanation.definitionFit: A rough cloth shirt of goat hair was worn by ascetics as self-punishment, literally a penitent's garment.

clue.text: Pretended to be distinguished

explanation.surface: Claiming falsely to be notable.
explanation.definitionFit: To make out is to claim or pretend, and also to discern or perceive something faintly.

clue.text: The poacher's fear is a Hindu psalm played softly

parts.note: a mantra is a sacred chant in Hinduism
p (piano) is the musical direction to play softly

explanation.surface: A poacher dreads a quiet Hindu hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: MANTRA then P, from piano, the musical term for soft.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap set to catch trespassers, which poachers on an estate had reason to dread.

clue.text: Don't let on how mother is often referred to

definitions.text: how mother is often referred to

explanation.surface: Keep it secret, and note what people call their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the phrase literally: the word for mother is often mum.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an injunction to keep quiet about a secret, and literally says mum is the usual term for mother.

clue.text: Publicity campaign to construct skyscrapers

explanation.surface: Promotion in advance of tall buildings going up.
explanation.definitionFit: A build-up is advance promotion of something, and to build up is literally to erect tall structures.

clue.text: Made a foreman lay the dynamite

explanation.surface: A promoted worker sets explosives on site.
explanation.definitionFit: Promoting someone to supervise others is to give them command, and laying explosives is inserting a blasting load.

clue.text: Leading Eastern American state

parts.note: main means chief or leading

explanation.surface: Naming a prominent state on the US east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is the north-easternmost state of the USA, in New England.

clue.text: Jeer after bowling sessions, but go too far

indicators.note: the jeering word is placed following the cricket word in the answer

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end
to hoot at someone is to jeer them

explanation.surface: A crowd jeers a bowler's spells, but the abuse goes too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the jeer behind the cricket term; an over is a set of six deliveries in cricket, Britain's bat-and-ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshoot is to pass beyond a target, literally to exceed what was meant.

clue.text: No agent misrepresented the weight of cargo

indicators.note: something misrepresented is distorted, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: No shipping agent lied about the freight's weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misrepresented' shuffles the seven letters of NO AGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage is a ship's cargo-carrying capacity or load, measured in tons.

clue.text: Bet seaman is prepared for humiliation

indicators.note: fodder that has been prepared is worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor braces himself to be shamed after a bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges the nine letters of BET SEAMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being degraded or brought low in dignity is humiliation, a synonym.

clue.text: Struck by a small glove

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a mitten is a glove without separate fingers

explanation.surface: Someone is hit with a little glove, as in a duel's challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Smitten is the old past participle of smite, meaning hit or struck, as well as infatuated.

clue.text: Get out an additional cent

parts.note: extra means additional
ct is an abbreviation for cent

explanation.surface: Someone tries to squeeze one more penny out of a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to draw or pull something out, as a tooth or juice.

clue.text: It appears in an article calling for church tax

indicators.note: the first word is said to show up within the next, so it goes inside

parts.note: an article is an object or thing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece demands a levy for the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears in' signals the container; 'article' looks like a newspaper item but means an object.
explanation.definitionFit: Tithing is paying a tenth of one's produce or income to support the clergy, a levy.

clue.text: Sees if one wants to buy fashions in store

definitions.text: Sees if one wants to buy

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so these letters are moulded into a new order

explanation.surface: A shopper checks garments on sale in the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashions' looks like clothes but is a verb rearranging IN STORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying on clothes is putting them on to check fit before purchase.

clue.text: Right EC regulation to achieve prosperity

indicators.note: regulation suggests the letters being ordered and arranged anew

explanation.surface: A correct European Community rule leads to wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regulation' rearranges RIGHT EC; EC is the old European Community.
explanation.definitionFit: To become wealthy is to attain prosperity.

clue.text: Highland massacre put sergeant in high spirits

indicators.note: the soldier is placed inside the word for merriment

parts.note: glee is joyful high spirits
a sergeant is an NCO, a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A massacre in the Highlands left a soldier elated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container. The 1692 slaughter of MacDonalds in the Scottish Highlands is named after this glen.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1692 slaughter of the MacDonald clan by government troops took place in this Scottish glen.

clue.text: I may write about German figures of speech

indicators.note: one piece is written around another, so it encloses it

parts.note: taken as written, the two words joined

explanation.surface: A writer considers composing about the language of Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'write about' puts GER inside I MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagery is figurative language: metaphors and similes collectively.

clue.text: At risk when using the telephone

explanation.surface: Danger while making a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Something staked or in jeopardy is at risk, and a caller connected by phone is on a phone circuit.

clue.text: Way to get publicity for one in flight

parts.note: St (street) is a word for a way or road
to get air or airtime is to get public exposure

explanation.surface: An airline passenger seeks attention on the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' is a flight of stairs, not air travel: one step is a member of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of steps is made up of individual treads, each a single step.

clue.text: It gives bodily strength to fresh wines

indicators.note: fresh suggests a new version, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: New wines are claimed to build up the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon that joins muscle to bone, and figuratively muscular power.

clue.text: Rex gains admittance to various clubs

indicators.note: the king gets entry into another word, going inside it

parts.note: divers is an old word for various or several
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king is admitted to several societies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gains admittance to' puts R inside DIVERS. Clubs are golf clubs, not societies.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers are golf clubs used for long tee shots.

clue.text: Gather there is no retired archdeacon in the Anglican church

indicators.note: the middle pieces are placed inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the word no is read backwards

parts.note: Ven, the Venerable, is an archdeacon's title

explanation.surface: A gathering of Anglicans without a retired archdeacon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns NO into ON; ON and VEN go 'in' CE, the Church of England, the Anglican church.
explanation.definitionFit: To convene is to assemble or come together for a meeting.

clue.text: Start to build a tunnel

explanation.surface: Beginning work on digging a tunnel.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the phrase literally: to tunnel is to get beneath a road.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin moving or proceed is the idiom's sense, and literally a tunnel goes below a road.
